# Draw on the motion.

FrameSketch is a video annotation tool that lets you sketch right on top of your footage.
Step through frames, mark up arcs and poses, and share the file.
No uploads. No lag. Just your lines, exactly where you left them.

Free to use. Your footage never leaves your device.

### Share the project

One small .fsk file holds every stroke. Email it, open it, keep going.

FEATURES

## Built for the way animators actually think.

No animation-suite bloat. Open a file, draw, get back to the shot.

### Frame-accurate

Lines land on the exact frame. Step forward, step back, scrub. The canvas never drifts from the video.

### Onion skin

Peek at the frames before and after. Tune the ghosting until it feels right.

### Strokes stay put

Lines are fixed the moment you lift the pen. Your marks stay exactly as drawn, frame after frame. [...] ### Notes and comments

Sticky notes and comment markers pinned right on the frame. Move, resize, recolor, and edit them anytime.

### Grid, rulers, and guides

Rectangular or isometric grids, drawn as dots or lines. Drag guides out of the rulers to line your marks up where you need them.

### Pan and zoom

Zoom into the detail, pan around the shot. Your marks stay exactly where you left them.

### Scenes and backgrounds

One project, many scenes. Every scene sits on a solid background layer, so you can hide or dim the video anytime.

WHY ANIMATORS STAY

## Private by default. Ready when you are.

FrameSketch runs entirely on your machine. Cloud sync is optional, and
it only carries annotations. Your footage never moves.

results.title: The 7 Best Frame.io Alternatives for Video Teams in 2026
results.content:
# So, Which Frame.io Alternative Is Right for You?

The best Frame.io alternative really depends on your team's workflow and priorities:

 If you're a creative agency or in-house team that needs a fast, intuitive review experience — especially one where non-technical clients can participate easily — Wipster is the strongest all-around choice. The unlimited reviewer model, editor panels, mobile access, and task-from-comment workflow cover everything most teams need at a price that scales sensibly.
 If you're enterprise with complex multi-stage approvals, look at Ziflow.
 If you produce lots of mixed media beyond video, Filestage is worth a look.
 If you're in animation or VFX, SyncSketch's annotation tools are hard to beat. [...] Starting price: Paid Plans starting at $199/month

Filestage positions itself as the review and approval platform for all creative assets — video, images, PDFs, audio, HTML banners, and more. If your team produces a wide range of content types and needs one tool to manage review across all of them, Filestage is worth considering.

Its free plan is genuinely useful for small teams, and the interface is clean and approachable. The main limitation compared to Wipster is that it's less video-native — frame-accurate commenting exists, but the experience is optimized more for documents and design files than for video-first teams.

Best for: Mixed-media creative and marketing teams reviewing diverse asset types.

# 4. SyncSketch — Best for Animation and VFX

Starting price: From $9/month [...] Starting price: From $9/month

SyncSketch is a specialized tool built for animation, VFX, and game development teams. Its standout feature is real-time whiteboard-style sketching directly over frames — reviewers can draw annotations, not just type text comments.

It's a niche tool for a specific use case, but in that niche, it's excellent. If your team does frame-by-frame visual work that requires drawn feedback rather than text-based comments, SyncSketch is probably your best option.

Best for: Animation studios, VFX houses, and game development teams.

# 5. Vimeo Review — Best for Teams Already in the Vimeo Ecosystem

Starting price: Included in Vimeo paid plans from ~$20/month

results.content:

This is quite similar to approach #2 above but it tries to eliminate the glaring video playback duration wait problem by performing `seek` instead of `play` while extracting out frames. Quite obvious really when you think about it.

In the current prototype, a predefined number of frames are unpacked, but this can also be easily changed to a frame-rate based approach rather than overall count.

Once frames are extracted, the scrubbing experience works the same.

Turns out, this is indeed much faster! On the same test setup, the same 15-second 1280x720p video took about 9 seconds to extract out 244 frames (first hit) and 6 seconds when the video was cached (subsequent hits). That’s a 2x-3x improvement for the same number of frames. [...] Initially, it seemed that downloading an image sprite with a bunch of frames as opposed to individual requests for every frame would a good idea, but it turned out to be very tricky. Based on the actual frame images and parameters like how many frames to fetch, sprites can actually degrade the performance by visibly increasing size of downloads or at least reduce flexibility. In a world with HTTP/2, distinct images fare better - we could even prioritise certain frames and bootstrap the scrubbing experience faster.

## #6: video-wasm-ffmpeg-extract

Definitely an idea to pursue, although I haven’t yet been able to test this in action.
